text:
Rajesh Kapoor: Hey team — noticed my Feb 25 paycheck is ~ $1,200 lower than expected, looks like CA state tax was withheld. I was working out of Reno, NV from Feb 3–16. NV has no state income tax — did payroll treat my worksite as CA?
Sam Liu: @Rajesh can you drop a screenshot of the paystub (redact anything extra) and confirm the exact travel dates?
Rajesh Kapoor: attaching screenshot (paystub snippet): Gross $8,000 | Federal $1,600 | CA State Withholding $1,200 | Net $5,200. Travel dates are Feb 3–16, back in SF Feb 17. I updated my address in HR portal last week but that was after the payroll cut.
Maya Patel: thanks — filing this now. Two quick Qs: 1) Did you submit a travel/worksite request in the Travel Form? 2) Are you still a CA resident for tax purposes or will you be filing as NV resident?
Rajesh Kapoor: I submitted a short-term travel note to my manager but not the formal Travel Form. I'm still CA resident, but physically worked from NV during that period.
Lina Gomez: FYI payroll policy: our automation changes withholding only for assignments >30 days or when Travel Form submitted/approved. Short trips default to home-state tax withholding unless manual override applied. Not saying it's correct for tax law, just how our system behaves.
PayrollBot: Payrun processed: PRN-4821 (2026-02-25). Tax jurisdiction: CA (home address). Automated rule: Worksite override requires TravelForm flag OR duration >= 30d.
Sam Liu: OK — looks like automation defaulted to CA because Travel Form wasn't flagged and duration <30d. We can do a manual retro adjustment to refund the state withholding if appropriate, but need: paystub screenshot, copy of manager approval or travel notes, and confirmation you'll handle any state filing impacts (CA may still assert resident taxation).
Rajesh Kapoor: manager (Lina) approved verbally — can Lina confirm? I can DM the calendar invite and manager note.
Lina Gomez: Confirmed — manager approved short assignment. I'll forward the calendar entry.
Sam Liu: Process steps I'll take once we have docs: 1) Create off-cycle adjustment to credit $1,200 as "state withholding refund - NV assignment". 2) Mark PRN-4821 for manual reconciliation and tag for payroll tax team. 3) Update employee worksite history so future short assignments can be flagged for manual review. Note: this will create an off-cycle net payment — typical ETA 3–7 business days.
Sam Liu: Also flagging for Tax Ops: if Rajesh remains CA resident, CA may disagree on withholding. We will document dates for payroll reconciliation. If CA requires withholding, we can still submit refund but Rajesh may need to file for refund when filing state return.
Rajesh Kapoor: Understood. I prefer payroll to issue the refund now and I'll handle any state filing consequences.
Sam Liu: Cool. Please DM the paystub and the calendar invite + manager confirm. I'll start the adjustment ticket.
PayrollBot: Ticket created: PRJ-PLY-9982 by Sam Liu — Off-cycle adj pending docs.
Maya Patel: Thanks all — Lina can you drop the calendar invite link here or DM Rajesh? Once Sam has docs I'll update the payroll case notes. :thumbsup:
Rajesh Kapoor: Sent DM w/ paystub + calendar link. Thanks!
Sam Liu: Got them. Kicking off adj, will update this thread when payment issued or if tax ops needs more info.
Lina Gomez: Added manager confirmation to the ticket.
Rajesh Kapoor: Appreciate it. Not urgent but wanted to catch before Q1 close.
Sam Liu: Noted — we'll prioritize since it's tax-period sensitive.
PayrollBot: Off-cycle adj scheduled: PRN-4821 -> Adj-2026-03-02-9982. ETA payout 2026-03-05.
Rajesh Kapoor: Great, thanks everyone.
Maya Patel: Closing loop once processed. If anything changes re: CA filing we'll follow up. :handshake:
